newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to sell Thomson-CSF in private placement.
newsitem.headline: France to sell Thomson-CSF in private placement.

text.p: The French government said on Wednesday it plans to privatise Thomson-CSF through a private placement with the aim of forming a big defence electronics grouping.
It said it was seeking to bring together many industrial capabilities around Thomson-CSF in the context of a restructuring of the European defence industry.

"It is open to the participation of French and European industrial players in this sector in the construction, in stages, around Thomson-CSF, of a big defence electronics grouping," a joint statement from the finance, defence and industry ministries said.
The sale will include a list of terms and conditions which will be submitted soon to the independent Privatisation Commission, the statement said.

By checking the terms of the sale with the Privatisation Commission at the outset, it should avoid a repeat of last year's debacle, when the government had to call off the sale at the last minute after the Commission objected to it.

The government is relaunching the privatisation of Thomson-CSF, 58 percent held by state-owned Thomson SA group, after having cancelled its previous plan to sell the entire group in one block in December.
The government had previously expressed a preference for a bid by Lagardere for the Thomson group over a rival bid by Alcatel Alsthom.
Thomson-CSF said it welcomed the government's decision because it answered some essential concerns about the sale.
A company spokesman said Thomson-CSF hoped the privatisation would take place as quickly as possible.
"The management of Thomson-CSF takes note of this decision and is pleased that it answers some essential concerns of Thomson-CSF," a spokesman told Reuters.

Thomson management was pleased by government's plan for Thomson-CSF to become a world-scale defence electronics company and welcomed the government's decision to retain a "golden share" to protect it.
Alcatel Alsthom said the government's decision to sell Thomson-CSF through a private placement went in the right direction.
Alcatel has acted to reinforce its position since last year by lining up a joint bid with state-owned aircraft and defence firm Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation for Thomson-CSF.
"It goes in the right direction," an Alcatel spokesman told Reuters. "We are awaiting the publication of the terms and conditions," he added.
Officials at Lagardere were not immediately available for comment.
France's decision to call off the sale last year caused a diplomatic row with South Korea, whose Daewoo Electronics had planned to buy Thomson Multimedia (TMM) from Lagardere.
The Privatisation Commission objected particularly to the involvement of Daewoo, which had been harshly criticised by French opposition politicians and TMM employees.
Forced to rethink, the government announced afterwards that it would sell its Thomson-CSF stake and TMM separately.
